config.otoroshi.io.GlobalConfig.description: The global configuration of otoroshi: the single, instance wide settings that apply to every request and to the whole instance (quotas, ip filtering, tls, analytics, alerts, global plugins, proxies, templates of the new entities...). It is a singleton, always read and written under the id `global`: it can be read and updated, not created nor deleted. A change applies at once to every instance of the cluster. The fields absent from a body take the value given in their description, which can differ from the one of a new instance (the template)

tags.description: The tags of the global configuration, free labels to search and organize the entities. Empty when absent

items.description: A tag

lines.description: The lines (environments, like `prod` or `preprod`) of the instance. Only used by the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility. `["prod"]` when absent

items.description: The name of a line

anonymousReporting.description: Send anonymous statistics about the instance (number of entities, enabled features, versions) to the otoroshi team, when the anonymous reporting is also enabled in the configuration of the instance (`otoroshi.anonymous-reporting.enabled`). `false` when absent

initWithNewEngine.description: Whether the instance was initialized for the proxy engine of the routes: its first start created the route that exposes the backoffice and the admin api. Informative once the instance has started. `true` for a new instance and when absent

maintenanceMode.description: Put every route in maintenance: every proxied request is answered with a 503 error instead of being forwarded, except the ones to the backoffice and the ones of the routes that turn the legacy checks off (metadata `otoroshi-core-apply-legacy-checks: false`). `false` when absent

enableEmbeddedMetrics.description: Compute the live metrics of the routes (calls, data in and out, durations) and store them in the datastore, for the backoffice. It performs many writes in the datastore. `true` when absent

streamEntityOnly.description: Not used anymore, the bodies are always streamed. Kept for compatibility. `true` when absent

autoLinkToDefaultGroup.description: Add a new service descriptor without group to the default group. Only used by the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility. `true` when absent

limitConcurrentRequests.description: Limit the number of requests handled at the same time by each instance to maxConcurrentRequests, the requests above being answered with a 429 error. Recommended for resilience. `false` when absent

maxConcurrentRequests.description: The maximum number of requests handled at the same time by each instance. Above it, an audit event and an alert are sent, and the requests are refused with a 429 error when limitConcurrentRequests is true. 1000 when absent

maxHttp10ResponseSize.description: The maximum size, in bytes, of a response to an HTTP/1.0 request: such a response is held in memory, the bytes above the limit are dropped. Choose it so that maxConcurrentRequests times maxHttp10ResponseSize fits in the memory of the process. 4194304 (4 MB) when absent

useCircuitBreakers.description: Always `true` and ignored on input: the circuit breakers are set on the backends of the routes since the service descriptors were removed

apiReadOnly.description: Freeze the datastore: the admin api and the backoffice refuse every call that is not a GET. It can then only be turned off directly in the datastore. The panic mode of the backoffice turns it on. `false` when absent

u2fLoginOnly.description: Disable the login to the backoffice through the auth module of backOfficeAuthRef: the admins log in with their otoroshi account only (login, password and their WebAuthn device when they have one). `false` when absent

superAdminWhenNoRights.description: Give the super admin rights to an admin or a user of the backoffice that has no rights at all. `false` for a new instance, `true` when absent (the instances that predate the flag, where missing rights meant super admin rights): turn it off before going live

trustXForwarded.description: Read the client address, the protocol and the host of the original request from the headers set by the reverse proxies in front of otoroshi (see trustedProxies and clientAddressHeader). When false, the address, protocol and host of the connection are used. `true` when absent

trustedProxies.description: The reverse proxies allowed to tell otoroshi who the client is: ip addresses, CIDR ranges or patterns where `*` matches anything. They are added to the ones given at startup (`OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `OTOROSHI_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `CC_REVERSE_PROXY_IPS`). When the list is not empty, the loopback is trusted too and the forwarded headers of anyone else are ignored; when it is empty, the forwarded headers of anyone are trusted. A single string is read as a one entry list, the entries that are not strings are left out

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern. An entry can hold a comma separated list, like a vault reference to an environment variable

clientAddressHeader.description: The header the client address is read from: `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded`, or any header holding the address like `X-Real-IP`. It must be one the reverse proxies build or overwrite. `OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADER` wins over this value when it is set. `X-Forwarded-For` when absent or blank

useLegacyClientIpAddress.description: Temporary way back to the resolution of the client address used before the trusted proxies: the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry, whoever sent it, when trustXForwarded is true, the address of the connection otherwise. Also turned on by `OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT_IP_ADDRESS=true`. Will be removed. `false` when absent

throttlingQuota.description: The maximum number of requests otoroshi handles, all clients together, during each throttling window (`app.throttlingWindow`, 10 seconds by default). The requests above are answered with a 429 error. 10000000 when absent

perIpThrottlingQuota.description: The maximum number of requests otoroshi handles for one client address during each throttling window (`app.throttlingWindow`, 10 seconds by default), unless the address has a quota of its own. The requests above are answered with a 429 error. 10000000 when absent

analyticsWebhooks.description: Legacy: the webhooks every analytics event is posted to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a webhook that cannot be read reads as empty

alertsWebhooks.description: Legacy: the webhooks every alert event is posted to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a webhook that cannot be read reads as empty

elasticWritesConfigs.description: Legacy: the Elasticsearch clusters every analytics event is written to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a config that cannot be read reads as empty

elasticReadsConfig.description: The Elasticsearch cluster the analytics shown by the backoffice and served by the analytics api are read from. null: no analytics are read. A config without any url reads as null

alertsEmails.description: The email addresses the alerts are sent to, through the mailer of mailerSettings. Empty when absent

items.description: An email address

logAnalyticsOnServer.description: Also write every analytics event to the logs of the instance. `false` when absent

useAkkaHttpClient.description: Use the Pekko (formerly Akka) http client for the http calls of otoroshi, the calls to the backends included, instead of the default client. `false` when absent

endlessIpAddresses.description: The client addresses answered with an endless response, about 128 GB of zeros or of middle finger emojis (see middleFingers), to waste the time of the bots: ip addresses, CIDR ranges or patterns where `*` matches anything. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

statsdConfig.description: The StatsD (or Datadog) agent the metrics of otoroshi are pushed to. null: none. A config without host or port reads as null

kafkaConfig.description: Legacy: the Kafka cluster every analytics and audit event is sent to. Prefer the data exporters. null: none. A config that cannot be read reads as null

backOfficeAuthRef.description: The id of the auth module the admins can log in to the backoffice with, on top of their otoroshi accounts. null: none

mailerSettings.description: The mailer otoroshi sends its emails with: the alerts to alertsEmails, the links of the users of the private apps... null: no email is sent. A config that cannot be read reads as null

cleverSettings.description: The credentials of the Clever Cloud api, to expose the applications of a Clever Cloud organization. null: none

maxWebhookSize.description: Not used anymore: the number of events posted at once to the analytics webhooks is set by `app.webhooks.size`. 100 when absent

middleFingers.description: Selects what the endless responses sent to endlessIpAddresses are made of: zeros, or middle finger emojis. `false` when absent

maxLogsSize.description: The maximum number of alert events and of audit events kept in the datastore, the older ones being dropped. 100 when absent, `app.events.maxSize` for a new instance (50 in the default configuration, 100 when it is not set)

otoroshiId.description: The unique id of the instance (of the whole cluster), set at its first start from `otoroshi.instance.instanceId` or to a random uuid. Sent with the anonymous reporting. A random uuid when absent

wasmoSettings.description: The wasmo server the wasm plugins are built by and fetched from. null: none. The legacy wasmManagerSettings key is read when wasmoSettings is absent or null

metadata.description: The metadata of the global configuration: free string keys and values. Empty when absent

env.description: Free json shared with the whole instance: read by the `local` vault (`vault://local/path/to/value`, a json pointer in this object), by the expression language (`${global_config.env.path}`, when `otoroshi.elSettings.allowGlobalConfigAccess` is true) and handed to the jobs. `{}` when absent

extensions.description: Settings stored in the global configuration by the admin extensions, each one under a key of its own (usually its id). `{}` when absent

additionalProperties.description: The settings of an admin extension, any json value

id.description: The id of the global configuration, always `global`: the global configuration is a singleton. The admin api adds it to the global configuration it answers, and ignores it on input

LetsEncryptSettings.description: The settings of the ACME client otoroshi uses to order and renew certificates from Let's Encrypt, or from any ACME server

enabled.description: Order and renew certificates through ACME. `false` when absent

server.description: The ACME directory: `acme://letsencrypt.org` for the Let's Encrypt production server, `acme://letsencrypt.org/staging` for its staging server (whose certificates no browser trusts), or the https url of the directory of any ACME server. `acme://letsencrypt.org/staging` when absent

emails.description: The email addresses of the ACME account, added to its contacts as `mailto:` urls: the ACME server sends them the notices about the account and its certificates. The blank entries are left out

items.description: An email address

contacts.description: Other contact urls of the ACME account, like `mailto:` urls. The blank entries are left out

items.description: A contact url

publicKey.description: The public key of the ACME account, PEM encoded. When the keys are empty, otoroshi generates an RSA 2048 key pair at the first order and saves it here. Empty when absent

privateKey.description: The private key of the ACME account, PEM encoded (PKCS#8). When the keys are empty, otoroshi generates an RSA 2048 key pair at the first order and saves it here. Empty when absent

preferredChain.description: The common name of the root certificate of the chain to deliver, when the ACME server offers several chains. null or blank: the default chain of the server

renewalPercentage.description: Renew a certificate once less than this percentage of its total lifetime remains. A value out of 1 to 100 reads as 20, the default

renewBeforeDays.description: Renew a certificate this number of days before it expires. It takes precedence over renewalPercentage, which degrades on short lived certificates. null: renewalPercentage applies. A value below 1 reads as null

deleteOldCertificatesAfterRenewal.description: Delete the previous certificate after a successful renewal, and the copies left by the previous renewals, instead of keeping a copy named `[UNTIL EXPIRATION]` until it expires. Only applies to the Let's Encrypt certificates. `false` when absent

IpFiltering.description: The client addresses allowed or refused on every request, before any route is looked for. An entry is an ip address (v4 or v6), a CIDR range (`10.0.0.0/8`) or a pattern where `*` matches anything (`192.168.1.*`). In each list, a single string is read as a one entry list and the entries that are not strings are left out

whitelist.description: The addresses allowed to call otoroshi. When the list is not empty, a client whose address matches no entry is refused with a 403 error. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

blacklist.description: The addresses refused with a 403 error. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

blacklistMatchesForwardedChain.description: Also refuse a request when a blacklisted address appears anywhere in the proxy chain of the client address header, not only when it is the resolved client address. Only applies while trustXForwarded is true. The client writes part of that chain, so it never applies to the whitelist. `false` when absent

Webhook.description: A webhook otoroshi posts events to, as json arrays of events

url.description: The url the events are posted to

headers.description: The http headers added to each call, for instance to authenticate it. Empty when absent

ElasticAnalyticsConfig.description: The connection to an Elasticsearch (or OpenSearch) cluster: the cluster events are written to, or the one the analytics are read from. A config without any url cannot be read

clusterUri.description: The first entry of uris, written for the clients of the legacy single url setting. On input it is still read, and added to uris

uris.description: The urls of the nodes of the cluster. An entry can hold a comma separated list of urls

items.description: The url of a node

index.description: The name of the index, or the prefix of the indexes when indexSettings.clientSide is true. null: `otoroshi-events`. Blank reads as null

type.description: The type of the documents, only needed by the Elasticsearch versions before 7. null: `event`. Blank reads as null

user.description: The user of the basic authentication on the cluster. null: no authentication. Blank reads as null

password.description: The password of the basic authentication on the cluster. Blank reads as null

headers.description: The http headers added to each call to the cluster, for instance an api key. Empty when absent

applyTemplate.description: Create or update the index template of otoroshi on the cluster before writing to it. `true` when absent

version.description: The version of the cluster. null or blank: it is asked to the cluster

maxBulkSize.description: The maximum number of events written by one bulk call. 100 when absent

sendWorkers.description: The number of bulk calls sent in parallel. 4 when absent

IndexSettings.description: How the events are indexed in Elasticsearch

action.description: The action of the bulk calls: `index`, or `create` to write to a data stream. `index` when absent

clientSide.description: Let otoroshi spread the events over one index per time interval, named `<index>-<date>`, instead of writing everything to a single index (for instance one rolled over by an ILM policy, or a data stream). `true` when absent

interval.description: The time interval each index covers, when clientSide is true. Read without case, an absent or unknown value reads as `Day`

numberOfShards.description: The number of primary shards of the indexes, set by the index template. 1 when absent

numberOfReplicas.description: The number of replicas of each shard, set by the index template. 1 when absent

StatsdConfig.description: The StatsD agent, or Datadog agent, the metrics of otoroshi are pushed to

host.description: The host name or the ip address of the agent the metrics are sent to, their names prefixed with `otoroshi`. A config with an empty host reads as null

port.description: The port the agent listens on, usually 8125

datadog.description: The agent is a Datadog agent: the metrics are sent with the extensions of Datadog. `false` when absent

KafkaConfig.description: The connection to a Kafka cluster otoroshi sends events to

servers.description: The bootstrap servers of the cluster. Empty when absent

items.description: A server, as `host:port`

keyPass.description: The password of the keystore and of the truststore, for the `SSL` and `SASL_SSL` protocols when mtlsConfig is not used. null: none

keystore.description: The path of the JKS keystore holding the client certificate, for the `SSL` and `SASL_SSL` protocols when mtlsConfig is not used. null: none

truststore.description: The path of the JKS truststore holding the certificates trusted to validate the brokers, for the `SSL` and `SASL_SSL` protocols when mtlsConfig is not used. null: none

topic.description: The topic the events are sent to. `otoroshi-events` when absent

sendEvents.description: Send the events to the cluster, for the legacy kafkaConfig of the global configuration: when false the connection is set up but nothing is sent. The data exporters always send their events. `false` when absent

hostValidation.description: Check that the certificates of the brokers match their host names, with the `SSL` and `SASL_SSL` protocols. `true` when absent

securityProtocol.description: The protocol used to talk to the brokers: `PLAINTEXT`, `SSL` (with the certificates of mtlsConfig, or with keystore and truststore), `SASL_PLAINTEXT` or `SASL_SSL` (authenticated with saslConfig). `PLAINTEXT` when absent

saslConfig.description: The SASL credentials, for the `SASL_PLAINTEXT` and `SASL_SSL` protocols. null: none

properties.description: Properties of the Kafka client set on top of the ones otoroshi computes. null: none

SaslConfig.description: The SASL authentication of a Kafka client

mechanism.description: The SASL mechanism: `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256` or `SCRAM-SHA-512`, or any mechanism of the Kafka client given with its jaasConfig. `PLAIN` when absent

jaasConfig.description: The JAAS configuration of the login module, used instead of the one built from username, password and mechanism. Only used with the `SASL_SSL` protocol. null: built from username, password and mechanism

MailerSettings.description: The mailer emails are sent with, selected by its `type`. An absent type reads as `none`, an unknown one as `console`

ConsoleMailerSettings.description: A mailer that only writes the emails to the logs of otoroshi, for tests

NoneMailerSettings.description: No mailer: the emails are dropped

GenericMailerSettings.description: A mailer calling an http api of your own: each email is posted as a json object with its `from`, `to`, `subject` and `html` fields

url.description: The url the emails are posted to

headers.description: The http headers added to each call, for instance to authenticate it. Empty when absent

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

MailgunSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of Mailgun

eu.description: Use the european api of Mailgun (`api.eu.mailgun.net`) instead of the american one. `false` when absent

apiKey.description: The api key of the Mailgun account

domain.description: The sending domain of the Mailgun account

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

MailjetSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of Mailjet

apiKeyPublic.description: The public api key of the Mailjet account

apiKeyPrivate.description: The private api key (secret key) of the Mailjet account

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

SendgridSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of SendGrid

apiKey.description: The api key of the SendGrid account

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

ScalewayTEMSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through Transactional Email, the email api of Scaleway

secretKey.description: The secret key of the Scaleway api key

projectId.description: The id of the Scaleway project the emails are sent from

region.description: The Scaleway region of the api. `fr-par` when absent or blank

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

MailPaceSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of MailPace

serverToken.description: The api token of the MailPace server (domain) the emails are sent from

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

EmailLocation.description: The recipient of an email. A plain string is read too, as the address used both as name and email

name.description: The display name of the recipient, sent along with the address (`name <email>`) by the mailers that support it

email.description: The address the emails are delivered to

CleverCloudSettings.description: The OAuth 1.0 credentials of a Clever Cloud application, used to call the api of Clever Cloud on an organization. The settings read as null unless all their fields are set and not empty

consumerKey.description: The consumer key of the OAuth 1.0 application

consumerSecret.description: The consumer secret of the OAuth 1.0 application

token.description: The OAuth 1.0 access token of the Clever Cloud user the api is called as, sent as `oauth_token`

secret.description: The secret of the access token, used with the consumer secret to sign the calls

orgaId.description: The id of the Clever Cloud organization

SnowMonkeyConfig.description: The settings of the snow monkey, the chaos engineering tool of otoroshi: each day, during its time window, it puts routes in outage, injecting faults (latency, errors, large bodies) in their traffic

enabled.description: Whether the snow monkey runs. Set by the start and stop operations of the snow monkey api. `false` when absent

outageStrategy.description: How the routes are put in outage: `OneServicePerGroup` picks one route of each group at a time, `AllServicesPerGroup` puts every route of a group in outage. An absent or unknown value reads as `OneServicePerGroup`

includeUserFacingDescriptors.description: Also put in outage the routes flagged as user facing. `false` when absent

dryRun.description: Only record the outages, without injecting any fault in the traffic. `false` when absent

timesPerDay.description: The number of outages of each group per day, spread over the time window. 1 when absent

startTime.description: The time of day the window of the snow monkey opens at, in the time zone of the instance. Written as `HH:mm:ss.SSS`, `HH:mm` and `HH:mm:ss` are read too. `09:00:00.000` when absent

stopTime.description: The time of day the window of the snow monkey closes at, in the time zone of the instance. Written as `HH:mm:ss.SSS`, `HH:mm` and `HH:mm:ss` are read too. `23:59:59.000` when absent

outageDurationFrom.description: The shortest duration of an outage, in milliseconds. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes)

outageDurationTo.description: The longest duration of an outage, in milliseconds. Defaults to 3600000 (1 hour)

targetGroups.description: The ids of the groups whose routes can be put in outage. Empty: every group

items.description: The id of a group

ChaosConfig.description: The faults the snow monkey injects in the traffic of a route in outage. Each fault is set, or null when it is not injected. A fault that cannot be read reads as null. Absent from a snow monkey config, it reads as enabled without any fault

largeRequestFaultConfig.description: Make the requests sent to the backends larger. null: not injected

largeResponseFaultConfig.description: Make the responses sent to the clients larger. null: not injected

latencyInjectionFaultConfig.description: Delay the responses. null: not injected

badResponsesFaultConfig.description: Answer error responses instead of calling the backends. null: not injected

LargeRequestFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that adds bytes to the body of the requests sent to the backends

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

additionalRequestSize.description: The number of bytes added to the body of an affected request

LargeResponseFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that adds bytes to the body of the responses sent to the clients

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

additionalResponseSize.description: The number of bytes added to the body of an affected response

LatencyInjectionFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that delays the responses by a random duration

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

from.description: The shortest delay added to an affected request, in milliseconds

to.description: The longest delay added to an affected request, in milliseconds

BadResponsesFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that answers an error response, picked at random, instead of calling the backend

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

responses.description: The responses an affected request can get

BadResponse.description: An error response answered by the snow monkey

status.description: The http status of the response. A string holding a number is read too. 500 when absent

body.description: The body of the response. `{"error":"..."}` when absent

headers.description: The http headers of the response. Empty when absent

GlobalScripts.description: Deprecated: the legacy scripts run on every request (transformers, validators, pre routings, sinks) and the legacy jobs. Use the plugins of the routes and the global plugins of plugins instead

enabled.description: Run the global scripts. `false` when absent

transformersRefs.description: The ids of the request transformer scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

transformersConfig.description: The configuration of the transformers, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

validatorRefs.description: The ids of the access validator scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

validatorConfig.description: The configuration of the validators, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

preRouteRefs.description: The ids of the pre routing scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

preRouteConfig.description: The configuration of the pre routings, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

sinkRefs.description: The ids of the request sink scripts, which answer the requests that match no route. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

sinkConfig.description: The configuration of the sinks, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

jobRefs.description: The ids of the job scripts run by the instance. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a job of the classpath

jobConfig.description: The configuration of the jobs, any json object: each job reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

GeolocationSettings.description: How the addresses of the clients are geolocated, selected by `type`: the location is added to the analytics events. An unknown type, or settings that cannot be read, read as `none`

MaxmindGeolocationSettings.description: The geolocation of the clients in a MaxMind city database (GeoLite2 or GeoIP2), loaded in memory

path.description: Where the database is loaded from: the path of a `.mmdb` file, or the http(s) url of a `.mmdb` file, of a `.zip` archive or of a `.tar.gz` archive holding it. Settings without a path read as `none`

IpStackGeolocationSettings.description: The geolocation of the clients through the api of ipstack

apikey.description: The access key of the ipstack account. Settings without an access key read as `none`

timeout.description: The timeout of a call to the api of ipstack, in milliseconds. 2000 when absent

UserAgentSettings.description: The extraction of the details of the user agent of the clients (browser, operating system, device), added to the analytics events

enabled.description: Parse the user agent of every request. It takes memory. `false` when absent

AutoCert.description: The certificates otoroshi generates on the fly, during the tls handshake, for the domains it has no certificate for

enabled.description: Generate a certificate, signed by the CA of caRef, for an allowed domain without certificate. `false` when absent

replyNicely.description: For a domain that is not allowed, still accept the tls connection with a generated certificate and answer an error page, instead of failing the handshake. `false` when absent

caRef.description: The id of the CA certificate the generated certificates are signed by

allowed.description: The domains a certificate can be generated for, `*` matching anything. Empty, no domain, for a new instance and when absent

items.description: A domain or a domain pattern

notAllowed.description: The domains no certificate is generated for, even when they match allowed, `*` matching anything. Empty when absent

items.description: A domain or a domain pattern

TlsSettings.description: The tls settings of the instance: the certificate used when none matches the domain of a connection, the CAs trusted on both sides, and the client authentication

defaultDomain.description: The domain whose certificate is used when no certificate matches the domain (SNI) of a tls connection. null or blank: none

randomIfNotFound.description: When no certificate matches the domain of a connection, nor defaultDomain, use the first available certificate. `false` when absent

includeJdkCaServer.description: Trust the CAs of the JDK to validate the client certificates of the incoming connections, and propose them in the certificate request of the handshake. `true` when absent

includeJdkCaClient.description: Trust the CAs of the JDK to validate the certificates of the servers otoroshi calls (backends, identity providers...). `true` when absent

trustedCAsServer.description: The ids of the CA certificates trusted to validate the client certificates of the incoming connections, the only CAs proposed in the certificate request of the handshake. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a CA certificate

bannedAlpnProtocols.description: The ALPN protocols never negotiated for some domains: the key is the domain (SNI) of the tls connection. Empty when absent

additionalProperties.description: The ALPN protocols refused for the domain

items.description: The id of an ALPN protocol, like `h2` or `http/1.1`

clientAuth.description: Whether the clients are asked for a certificate during the tls handshake, on the listeners whose client authentication is `Dynamic` (the default of `otoroshi.ssl.fromOutside.clientAuth`): `None` never, `Want` asked but optional, `Need` required. Read without case, `Dynamic`, an absent or an unknown value reads as `None`

strictBackendServerValidation.description: Strictly validate the certificates of the backend servers on the mTLS calls (targets with a tls config enabled): the untrusted certificates and the ones whose host name does not match are refused, and trustAll takes precedence. Only used when `otoroshi.ssl.trust.strictBackendServerValidation` is `global` (the default). `true` for a new instance, `false` when absent, to keep the historical permissive behavior of the existing configs

QuotasAlmostExceededSettings.description: The alerts sent when the consumption of an api key gets close to its daily or monthly quota

enabled.description: Send an alert when the consumption of an api key crosses a threshold. `false` when absent

dailyQuotasThreshold.description: The share of its daily quota an api key consumes before an alert is sent, between 0 and 1. 0.8 when absent

monthlyQuotasThreshold.description: The share of its monthly quota an api key consumes before an alert is sent, between 0 and 1. 0.8 when absent

Plugins.description: The global plugins, run on every request: the legacy plugins of refs, and, through config, the plugins of the proxy engine and its settings

enabled.description: Run the legacy plugins of refs on every request. `false` when absent

refs.description: The ids of the legacy plugins run on every request. A new instance runs the proxy engine of the routes, `cp:otoroshi.next.proxy.ProxyEngine`. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a plugin: `cp:` followed by its class name for a plugin of the classpath

config.description: The configuration of the global plugins, any json object. `ng` holds the plugins of the proxy engine run on every request (a list of plugin instances, like the plugins of a route), `NextGenProxyEngine` the settings of the proxy engine, `incoming_request_validators` the validators of every incoming request, and the other keys the configuration of the legacy plugins of refs, under their configuration root. `{}` when absent

excluded.description: The regular expressions of the paths of the requests the legacy plugins of refs are not run on. An entry `only:<plugin id>:<regex>` only excludes that plugin. Empty when absent

items.description: A regular expression matching the whole path of a request, or `only:<plugin id>:<regex>`

Proxies.description: The http proxies the calls of otoroshi go through, one per kind of call. null: the calls are direct. A proxy without host or port reads as null

alertEmails.description: The proxy of the calls to the apis of the mailers

eventsWebhooks.description: The proxy of the calls to the webhooks of the events

clevercloud.description: The proxy of the calls to the api of Clever Cloud

services.description: The proxy of the calls to the backends of the routes, of their health checks and of the traffic mirroring

auth.description: The proxy of the calls to the identity providers of the auth modules (OAuth2, OIDC)

authority.description: The proxy of the calls to the remote validation authorities (client certificate validators, external validations)

jwk.description: The proxy of the calls fetching the JWKS of the jwt verifiers

elastic.description: The proxy of the calls to Elasticsearch

TlsWasmoSettings.description: The connection to a wasmo server, the builder of the wasm plugins otoroshi fetches and runs. The legacy flat form, the settings alone, is read too

tlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to wasmo, used when the tlsConfig of settings is null or not enabled. A config with `settings` but without `tlsConfig` reads as the default wasmo settings, the given settings being dropped

WasmoSettings.description: The address and the credentials of a wasmo server

url.description: The url of the wasmo server. `http://localhost:5001` when absent

clientId.description: The client id otoroshi authenticates on wasmo with. `admin-api-apikey-id` when absent

clientSecret.description: The client secret otoroshi authenticates on wasmo with. `admin-api-apikey-secret` when absent

legacyAuth.description: Authenticate with the legacy `Otoroshi-User` header, a jwt signed with clientId, instead of a basic authentication with clientId and clientSecret. `false` when absent

pluginsFilter.description: The kind of the plugins listed from wasmo, sent in the `kind` header of the calls, `*` for every kind. `*` when absent; null is kept and lists every kind too

tlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to wasmo, read from tlsConfig, tls or tls_config. null: the tlsConfig of the enclosing wasmo settings applies

WasmoTlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to a wasmo server (the tls config of the wasm4s library)

certs.description: The ids of the certificates presented as client certificates. A single id given as `certId` or `cert_id` is read too. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a certificate

trusted_certs.description: The ids of the certificates trusted to validate the certificate of the server. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a certificate

enabled.description: Use these tls settings for the calls. `false` when absent

loose.description: Do not check the host name of the certificate of the server. `false` when absent

trust_all.description: Trust any certificate of the server. For tests only. `false` when absent

DefaultTemplates.description: Json objects deep merged into the template the api serves for each kind of new entity (the `_template` operations, the new entities of the backoffice), to give the new entities of the instance defaults of their own. A null or empty template leaves the template unchanged. A string holding the json of the whole object is read too

route.description: Merged into the template of the new routes

service.description: Merged into the template of the new route compositions

backend.description: Merged into the template of the new backends

target.description: Not used yet: no template of a target reads it

descriptor.description: Merged into the template of the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility

apikey.description: Merged into the template of the new api keys

group.description: Merged into the template of the new service groups

template.description: Not used yet: no template of an error template reads it

verifier.description: Merged into the template of the new jwt verifiers

authConfig.description: Merged into the template of the new auth modules

certificate.description: Merged into the template of the new certificates

script.description: Merged into the template of the new scripts and of the new wasm plugins

draft.description: Merged into the template of the new drafts

api.description: Merged into the template of the new apis

tcpService.description: Merged into the template of the new tcp services

dataExporter.description: Merged into the template of the new data exporters

tenant.description: Merged into the template of the new organizations (tenants)

team.description: Merged into the template of the new teams

apiSubscription.description: Merged into the template of the new api subscriptions

routeTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new route templates

userDashboardTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new user dashboards

userAlertTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new user alerts
